items.title: Omamobile: Omarchy on a Pixel phone, and not an official project
items.content_text: An independent project’s fourth release runs Omarchy on a Pixel 7 Pro with no Android underneath. It is a developer preview.

angles.angle: A phone is one of the places.
The phone people are building in the open.

claims.text: Omamobile is an independent community project, not an official Omarchy project.
It was renamed because Omarchy’s author asked that it not be called Omarchy Mobile.
The release of 24 November is a developer preview for one phone, the Pixel 7 Pro.
It runs Omarchy’s own packages on a mainline Linux kernel, with no Android underneath.
Calls, texts and mobile data work on the one network tested so far.
Installing erases the phone’s data.
Voice typing runs on the phone, and what you say stays there.
The app drawer follows your finger up, and home pages settle in at most 250 milliseconds.
Other phones are being brought up in the same repository, more Pixels and two OnePlus phones among them.
GitHub lists Derek Ross and W4HO-ham as its two largest contributors; W4HO-ham’s recent work is the Pixel 9a.

to_find: A second network tested
Someone using it as their only phone
_omarchy_news.would_change: A release for a second phone.

items.title: The install race: 18 seconds, six, then 4.79
items.content_text: DHH posts an install under five seconds, with encryption on. The code says what the clock counts and where the time went.

angles.angle: Speed as a headline.
The seconds, and the code that removed them.

claims.text: Six seconds on a Ryzen 7 9800X3D with 32 GB of memory.
Eighteen seconds on the N1X.
The installer screen in the photo reads: Installed Omarchy in 0m 18s.
Omarchy can install in less than five seconds on an AMD 495 machine that Anush Elangovan gave DHH.
The installer screen in the photo reads: Installed Omarchy in 4.79s.
The sub-five-second install had encryption on.
The clock starts when the installer begins its first step, after the questions, and stops after its last, the factory snapshot.
Starting from the stick, answering the questions and the restart are not on the clock.
Preparing the machine’s package keys was 3.72 seconds of a 9.27-second install on a Framework 13, so that work now starts before the disk is written.
The slow step that protects the disk password now overlaps with the setup that follows the disk write.
A first try that set the password’s cost earlier chose a password 20 to 35 percent cheaper to attack, so it was left out.
The six-second run was posted by washinkoko.
On that change, the project’s automatic install test took 15.7 seconds on x86, 4.3 less than before, and 23 seconds on ARM, 2.8 more.
claims.who: the test posted on the change

to_find: A measurement by someone else of the 4.79-second build
Which release carries it
A source for how fast the hardware could go
_omarchy_news.would_change: An independent timing.

items.title: GNOME withdraws a proposed AI policy
items.content_text: A project-wide policy on generative AI was proposed on November 19 and withdrawn by its author on November 23.

angles.angle: Who sets the rules when volunteers, donors and corporate partners disagree.
The partner money behind a rules decision.

claims.text: The proposal allowed private AI use, barred AI-made code, documentation, issues and reviews, and let projects opt out.
The author formally withdrew it at 14:36 UTC on November 23 and gave no reason in that post.
At 12:23 UTC the same day Allan Day raised concerns, including corporate partnerships worth $736,000 in the last financial year; later that day Day put donations at about $230,000.

At 14:33 UTC, three minutes before the withdrawal, Allan Day said it was not possible to say the policy would definitely drive partners away, and added: “But it’s certainly not going to help us keep them.”
Allan Day is listed by the GNOME Foundation as Interim Executive Director.
None of the 184 posts read names Omarchy or DHH.

to_find: The closed merge request and any reason its author gives there
A supporter of the policy in their own words after the withdrawal
The three posts our reader did not return (184 of 187)
Whether “total ban”, the Lunduke Journal’s description, is fair given the opt-out
_omarchy_news.would_change: A statement from the author giving a reason, or a new proposal.

items.title: M4 and M5 Macs boot in developer builds
items.content_text: A merged installer change gives newer Macs a boot path. It is held to edge images and the developer catalog.

angles.angle: The newest Macs, and how far they have got.
The Mac installer learns the M4.

claims.text: A merged change gives M4 and later Macs their own way to boot.
On a test build, an M4 Pro MacBook Pro came up with all 14 cores, Wi-Fi, Touch ID, camera, speakers and an external display.
An M5 MacBook Air boots, from an earlier version of the work.
The change reaches edge images and the developer catalog only.
The exact build that was merged had not been installed on hardware when the change was written up.
The change was merged on 22 November by Marcelo Alcantara and written by Scott Jones.
When the change was written up, no catalog could offer an M4 for an ordinary install.

items.title: What the $24 million is made of
items.content_text: The announced pledges add up to $23.87 million, which agrees with the stated total of about $24 million. Cash received is not published on the pages read.

angles.angle: The sum, taken apart.
About a sixth of it is AI tokens and compute.

claims.text: Twelve founders at $1M: $12M. DigitalOcean and Alibaba Cloud at $3M, and 1Password, 37signals, Four Technologies and Beelink at $300K: $7.2M. Tokens from Meta, SpaceXSI, OpenAI, Fireworks, OpenRouter, OrcaRouter and Greptile: $3.75M. Namespace compute: $0.3M. Five people at $100K, plus open patronage at a stated $120K: $0.62M.
A critic’s page calls the total a pile of promises: one-time gifts, multi-year commitments and donor-priced tokens.
Everything raised this year is to be spent over the following three.

to_find: Cash received, from the foundation
The Register’s article, read in full
The critic’s account that one token patron left the September 3 announcement, checked against a primary source
_omarchy_news.would_change: A financial statement, or a new or withdrawn patron.
